Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a draft MAP (xlsx) and a concise tech evaluation runbook (PDF) plus a representative eval dataset (JSONL) we propose to use. Summary of the technical evaluation milestone below.

Technical evaluation milestone (summary):
- Objective: Validate that Redwood inference meets Acme's latency and cost SLOs while preserving answer quality on domain-specific prompts.
- Success criteria (pass/fail):
  * Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for 256-token prompts; <= 400ms for 512-token end-to-end (including network to the region we propose: us-west-2).
  * Throughput: sustained 15 QPS per dedicated instance with 99% of requests under latency targets (with batching turned on as configured).
  * Cost: production unit cost target of <= $0.004 per 1k tokens served (measured on the benchmark harness with typical prompt lengths).
  * Quality: top-line accuracy / correctness on the eval set >= 86%; hallucination rate <= 5% (measured by our shared eval dataset and rubric).
  * Stability: no out-of-memory or model crashes during a 4-hour continuous run under the target load.

- Model shortlist (recommended order):
  1) Mistral-Instruct-7B (fp16 & 4-bit quantized variants) — best cost/latency balance for instruction tasks
  2) Llama2-70B (8-bit quantized variant) — quality baseline for complex reasoning prompts
  3) Falcon-40B-Instruct (fp16) — strong open-instruction performance; falls in between on cost/latency
  4) Redwood-verified optimized variant (if available) — fallback with predictable latency profile

- Benchmark harness & dataset: use attached eval_dataset_v2.jsonl (500 representative prompts across knowledge, instruction, and retrieval-augmented scenarios). We'll run both generation and RAG-style retrieval latencies where applicable.

- Environment & config assumptions:
  * Region: us-west-2 (we can mirror eu-west-1 if needed later)
  * Instance types: dedicated GPU pool (A100 equivalent) for baseline fp16 runs; T4/RTX-class for quantized runs
  * Batching: continuous batching with max batch size 8 for latency tests; throughput tests will use batching up to 32 to measure cost/throughput tradeoffs
  * KV-cache warmup: 5 minute warmup before measurements

- Timeline & responsibilities (draft):
  * 2026-06-28: Finalize MAP and sign-off on eval dataset (owner: Acme - Sophie; Redwood owner: Marissa)
  * 2026-07-01: Start benchmark window (owner: Redwood - Rishi; Acme: Tom to allocate eng time for observation)
  * 2026-07-02 to 2026-07-03: Run benchmarks and gather logs/metrics (owner: Redwood - Rishi)
  * 2026-07-05: Deliver results, analysis, and recommended config (owner: Redwood - Marissa / Rishi)
  * Dependencies: access to any private prompt templates or retrieval index (if you want RAG tests), NDA signed if dataset contains PII.

Next steps: please review the attached MAP and runbook and tell us if the success criteria or timeline need adjustments. Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call to finalize.

Thanks —

Hi team — adding technical detail and run instructions from the SE side. A few clarifications and options: 

1) Latency targets: the p95 numbers Marissa proposed are conservative for fp16 on A100; for quantized 4-bit we expect slightly lower memory usage and comparable latency but we will validate. If Acme needs p50-focused SLAs instead, let us know.

2) Cost measurement: we will compute tokenized system + user tokens and report cost normalized to 1k tokens. Note that quantized variants often reduce infra cost by ~25-40% in practice.

3) Model selection guidance: we recommend running the shortlist in this order to minimize run time (start with Mistral-Instruct-7B quantized, then move up to Falcon-40B, then Llama2-70B as quality upper bound).

4) Required inputs from Acme:
  - A canonical prompt set or templates (we provided a starter in eval_dataset_v2.jsonl).
  - Access to any retrieval index if you want RAG tests (S3 or snapshot).
  - Confirmation of the target token lengths (we used 256 / 512 as suggested).

5) Runbook highlights (attached):
  - Setup script (one-liner) to spin required infra in our dedicated pool for the benchmark run
  - Measurement script outputs (latency percentiles, cost per 1k tokens, output diffs for quality checks)
  - Post-run artifacts we will deliver: raw traces, per-prompt outputs, hallucination annotations, and a short slide with recommendation.

I'll be available to run the tests the week of July 1st. If you want us to include noise/dirty-input runs (to stress hallucination), say the word.

— Rishi
